intro: The collective is an international network of researchers working in the fields of education, art, craft, culture & technology
heading: Members

items.name: Tomi Slotte Dufva
items.role: Assistant Professor in Arts Education; group coordinator
items.institution: Aalto University, the School of Arts, Design and Architecture, Department of Art and Design

image.alt: Portrait of Tomi Slotte Dufva wearing translucent glasses

items.researchInterests: Post-digital, post-AI art, education and culture; embodied and experiential learning; critical digital literacy; visual culture; philosophies of art, craft, and education
items.bio: Tomi Slotte Dufva coordinates the group and researches art, education, culture, and technology through post-digital and post-AI perspectives, with attention to embodiment, experience, critical literacy, visual culture, and philosophies of art, craft, and education.

items.name: Iiro Tujula
items.role: Multidisciplinary artist, designer and educator; doctoral researcher
items.institution: Aalto University and Velkua Comprehensive School

image.alt: Illustrated avatar of Iiro Tujula holding colorful art and technology objects

items.researchInterests: Art and technology; creative learning; visual technologies; digital making; multidisciplinary art and education
items.bio: Iiro works across artistic practice, design, and education. Alongside doctoral research at Aalto University, he teaches visual arts and craft at Velkua Comprehensive School and explores how technologies participate in creative learning.

items.name: Roberto
items.institution: Academy of Fine Arts, University of the Arts Helsinki

image.alt: Portrait of Roberto standing beside a textured wall

items.researchInterests: Sensors, data and simulation; feedback systems; sonification; experimental electronics; programming and design
items.bio: Roberto is a Helsinki-based media artist working with sensors, data, and simulation to explore the Baltic Sea and other environmental systems. His practice treats technology as an instrument that can shape experience, while remaining attentive to the social and ethical conditions surrounding technological work.

items.name: Ingrid Forsler
items.role: Associate Professor in Media and Communication Studies

image.alt: Portrait of Ingrid Forsler standing outdoors

items.researchInterests: Postdigital media; digital sociability in education; visual arts teacher education; interactive research methodologies
items.bio: Ingrid is a media and communication researcher with a background in visual arts education. Her work examines current digital sociability in education, teacher education reform, and the histories and futures of interactive research methodologies.

items.name: Tiago Martins Pinto
items.role: Doctoral Researcher in Art Education; Workshop Master in ARTS IT

image.alt: Black-and-white portrait of Tiago Martins Pinto

items.researchInterests: Digital technology in art and education; informal media-based learning; participation; facilitation; creative practice with young people
items.bio: Tiago works across digital technology, educational practice, and creative coding. His doctoral research focuses on informal artistic and media-based learning with immigrant-background young people in Eastern Helsinki, particularly questions of participation, facilitation, and creative practice.

items.name: Ingri Strand
items.role: Associate Professor in Digital Development in Design, Art and Crafts Education
items.researchInterests: Virtual reality and AI in art and crafts education; architectural tasks; screen-based media; interdisciplinary pedagogy
items.bio: Ingri develops pedagogy in design, art, and crafts education in relation to new technologies. Her research includes virtual reality in lower-secondary architectural tasks and the introduction of technologies such as VR and AI into art and crafts education.

items.name: DanTommi
items.role: Artist, art educator and artistic researcher
items.researchInterests: Physical, digital and virtual spaces; sculpture; photography; photogrammetry; 3D scanning; public clouds; visual environments
items.bio: DanTommi's practice moves between physical, digital, and virtual spaces. Working with sculpture, photography, photogrammetry, 3D scanning, public clouds, and virtual environments, DanTommi explores how spaces become digital and how digital forms return to physical space.

items.name: Hanna
items.institution: Lucerne University of Applied Sciences and Arts (HSLU), Switzerland

image.alt: Portrait of Hanna making a hand gesture

items.researchInterests: Creative coding; art and media education; web cultures; software studies; computer aesthetics; postdigital subjectivation
items.bio: Hanna teaches across hybrid bachelor modules in design, film, and art. Her doctoral work reconstructs creative coding from an art and media education perspective, asking how practitioners navigate its heterogeneous positions, assumptions, and unresolved questions.

items.name: Kasperi Mäki-Reinikka
items.role: University Teacher in Art Education; doctoral researcher

image.alt: Portrait of Kasperi Mäki-Reinikka in front of a projected image

items.researchInterests: Art, science, and technology; interdisciplinary dialogue; collaboration; media art; art education
items.bio: Kasperi is a university teacher in art education and a doctoral researcher at Aalto University. With a background in school art teaching, media art, and arts organizations, he studies how dialogue and collaboration across art and science can have a systemic impact on postdigital society.

items.name: Pekka Mertala
items.role: Associate Professor of Multiliteracies and Digital Literacies

image.alt: Portrait of Pekka Mertala wearing glasses

items.researchInterests: Postdigital childhood; education, texts, and technologies; new literacies; human-computer interaction; relational philosophy
items.bio: Pekka studies what it means to be a child in a postdigital world. He leads the interdisciplinary Education, Texts, and Technologies research group and currently explores how different forms of talent are defined, recognized, and performed in postdigital conditions.

items.name: Lauri Palsa

image.alt: Lauri Palsa photographed outdoors in an orchard

items.researchInterests: Literacies; media and data literacy; education policy; digital technologies in learning; ecological and social dimensions of educational technology
items.bio: Lauri works with media literacy, data literacy, and education research across national and European contexts. His postdoctoral work considers how literacy concepts are reshaped in the postdigital age, with particular attention to the ecological and social dimensions of educational technology.
